questions.question: Explain how the Portuguese explored the west coast of Africa step by step.
questions.expected_answer: From the 1430s, Portuguese ships sailed a little further south on each voyage. Gil Eanes passed Cape Bojador in 1434, ships crossed the equator in the 1470s, and Diogo Cão reached the Congo River and placed a padrão at Cape Cross in Namibia in about 1486. Each voyage brought back maps and knowledge of winds, currents and harbours, and sailors learnt to swing out into the Atlantic to avoid the Benguela Current and southerly winds.

questions.question: Describe how Bartolomeu Dias rounded the southern tip of Africa in 1488.
questions.expected_answer: Dias left Lisbon in 1487 with two caravels and a supply ship. Early in 1488, a storm blew his ships far south out of sight of land. When he turned north, he found the coast running west to east, so he had passed the tip without seeing it. He landed at Mossel Bay and sailed as far as the area near Kwaaihoek before his crew made him turn back. On the way home he saw the cape that the King of Portugal named the Cape of Good Hope.

questions.question: Describe the sea route to the East and explain why the Cape was important to it.
questions.expected_answer: Ships sailed from Lisbon south past the Canary and Cape Verde islands, swung out into the Atlantic, rounded the Cape, sailed up the east coast of Africa to Swahili towns such as Mombasa and Malindi, and crossed the Indian Ocean with the monsoon to India, a voyage of about six months or more. The Cape was roughly halfway, so ships stopped there for fresh water, meat from the Khoikhoi, repairs and good winds.
